items.excerpt: Norway's government said Monday it will introduce a law for a temporary ban on AI glasses in places such as parks, beaches, schools and kindergartens, and set up an expert group to draft permanent rules.

Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) sent a letter Monday urging Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei against an 'alarmist approach' and 'panic-inducing commentary' on AI, according to Axios, ahead of Anthropic's expected IPO.

Nvidia-backed startup Reflection is preparing a powerful American open-weight model positioned as an alternative to Chinese open models as well as US closed labs (Axios scoop). Geopolitics angle: US vs China open-weight competition; business-leaning.
China has plenty of AI safety talent, but weak philanthropy and a strong state shape what type of safety work actually gets done.

CSET's Josh A. Goldstein and Renee DiResta (Foreign Affairs op-ed) examine how foreign influence operations are evolving as governments combine traditional propaganda, social media, covert networks, influencers and AI.
Since 2025 Tokyo has moved to ward off foreign AI-related threats by developing AI 'for Japan, in Japan' -- an assessment of Japan's sovereign-AI push against China's dominance.
How Asia-Pacific governments are navigating a new era of resource regulation for AI data centers (power, water, siting).
FPF argues there is no standardized way to evaluate privacy risks in frontier AI and lays out how privacy benchmarks could become a governance tool as systems grow more autonomous.
Generative AI can increase the quantity and quality of malign foreign influence campaigns. However, questions remain as to whether these campaigns influence public opinion.
Fifty European Union lawmakers, including 46 women, have been the targets of deepfake pornography, according to new research released Monday. The number of women targeted by deepfake pornography — …
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told POLITICO's Decoded the world should accept some bad things happening for AI's benefits, distinguishing his policy stance from rival Anthropic. Interview/commentary.

OpenAI is launching 'textGrain' text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex in the EU to meet EU AI Act transparency requirements, but says it won't be the global default yet; Anthropic made a similar move.
Decoder interview: Sen. Adam Schiff on how Congress could regulate AI, free speech and federal preemption. Interview format.
New Jersey's former lieutenant governor, who resigned over a sexual harassment investigation, is citing an AI analysis to insist on his innocence -- AI used as a tool of political persuasion.
Under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act,  data center projects in rural areas could be eligible for major tax benefits starting next year. Some hyperscalers do not seem eager to take the free cash.
ChatGPT-generated fake New Yorker cartoons are carrying real cartoonists' signatures, raising attribution, provenance and copyright concerns as the images spread virally.
Maia Woluchem, Ana Carolina de Assis Nunes and Hannah Sassaman on why Pennsylvania communities are resisting AI data centers.

Mark Scott: Brussels is postponing parts of the AI Act and cutting tech red tape via the digital omnibus while proposing new rules like the EU Kids Act, exposing a tension in Europe's digital agenda. Analysis.
Petra Molnar on a major Greece-Israel defense tech deal and who EU states buy AI surveillance and weapons from, noting the EU AI Act excludes military/national security uses.
AI agents introduce new cyber risk, liability and governance questions that organizations should consider carefully.
